task: Add a default Authority trust/client bundle generator with an explicit senior opt-in variant and legacy filename aliases.
outcome: A developer can get the default `lattice_authority_trust.env` and `lattice_staging-client.env` bundle without extra fields, an explicit senior opt-in can emit `lattice_senior_authority_trust.env` and `lattice_senior_staging-client.env`, and the legacy `authority_trust.env` / `staging-client.env` names keep working as compatibility aliases.
facts: Existing code already reads `authority_trust.env` in enforce mode, so the new work must preserve that path.
The user wants ordinary developers to have one obvious bundle by default, with senior mode as an explicit opt-in.
Legacy `authority_trust.env` and `staging-client.env` names must keep working as compatibility aliases.
This story is about simplifying the credential bundle workflow, not redesigning tenant auth or multi-tenant management.
constraints: Do not optimize for the sake of optimization.
Do not add multi-tenant or unrelated auth redesign work.
Keep secret material out of logs and docs.
Preserve legacy compatibility while introducing the Lattice-prefixed names.
unknowns: Exact generator entry point and file emission mechanism.
Whether senior mode is toggled by a flag or a separate command.
Which docs need updates beyond the immediate authority bundle decision notes.
